name: Maryland
note: The attending physician, PA or nurse practitioner (or the medical examiner, for reportable deaths) completes the medical part of the certificate within 24 hours, and the mortician files it within 72 hours of death, by paper or an approved electronic process. The mortician must hold a burial-transit permit before disposition, and the cemetery returns it to the Secretary of Health within ten days. The Maryland Department of Health reports deceased residents to the State Board of Elections, which also takes SSA death data, and local boards remove voters after a notice period. Certified copies go only to persons with a direct and tangible interest under COMAR, a list that expressly includes insurers, pension payers, creditors and others proving a death, and the Motor Vehicle Administration as well as local health departments can issue them.

citations.title: Determination of death
citations.quote: An individual is dead if, based on ordinary standards of medical practice, the individual has sustained either:

citations.title: Certificate of death — who fills out and signs
citations.quote: A certificate of death regardless of age of decedent shall be filled out and signed by:

citations.title: Certificate of death — medical certification deadline
citations.quote: The medical certification shall be completed within 24 hours after receipt of the death certificate by the physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner

citations.title: Certificate of death — electronic attestation
citations.quote: shall attest to the accuracy by signature or by an approved electronic process

citations.title: Certificate of death — notice to medical examiner
citations.quote: Each individual concerned with carrying out this subtitle promptly shall notify the medical examiner if:

citations.title: Certificate of death — delivery to mortician
citations.quote: A physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner who fills out a certificate of death shall give it or transmit it by approved electronic media

citations.title: Certificate of death — mortician files
citations.quote: A mortician who obtains a certificate of death under this section shall file the certificate within 72 hours after the death.

citations.title: Medical examiner — report on cause of death
citations.quote: the medical examiner who investigates the case shall file in the medical examiner’s office a report on the cause of death within 30 days

citations.title: Burial-transit permit
citations.quote: the mortician who first takes custody of the body or fetus shall obtain a burial–transit permit

citations.title: Burial-transit permit — return by cemetery
citations.quote: Within 10 days after final disposition, return the permit to the Secretary.

citations.title: Certified copies
citations.quote: the Secretary shall provide, on request, any person authorized by regulations adopted under this subtitle with a certified or abridged copy

citations.title: Certified copies — local health departments and MVA
citations.quote: a local health department or the Motor Vehicle Administration may:

citations.quote: a notice which advises that certain individuals may be entitled to continuation of group health insurance benefits

citations.title: Inspection of records and disclosure of information
citations.quote: issue certified copies of vital records, original certificates, or information when satisfied that the applicant has a direct and tangible interest

citations.quote: whenever a local board becomes aware of an obituary or any other reliable report of the death of a registered voter

steps.title: Determination of death
steps.who: A practitioner applying ordinary standards of medical practice; the statute does not list who may pronounce.
steps.summary: Death is irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions or of all brain functions, and must be pronounced before any vital organ is removed for transplantation.

steps.title: Prompt notice to the medical examiner
steps.who: Every individual concerned with the certificate (clinician, mortician, carrier).
steps.trigger: No treating clinician during the terminal illness, unknown cause, or accident, homicide, suicide, other external cause, alcoholism or criminal abortion.
steps.summary: In these cases the medical examiner takes charge, signs the certificate, may enter 'investigation pending' after 24 hours, and later reports the cause to the Secretary.

steps.title: Clinician or medical examiner completes the medical certification
steps.who: The physician, physician assistant or nurse practitioner who last attended (or associate, institution's chief medical officer, autopsy physician); or the medical examiner if it took charge.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the death certificate from the mortician.

deadline.text: within 24 hours after receipt of the death certificate; to the mortician within 24 hours after death

steps.summary: The certifier enters only name, cause, date/hour and place of death, attests by signature or an approved electronic process, and gives or electronically transmits it to the mortician.

steps.title: Mortician files the death certificate
steps.who: The mortician (or person acting as such) who has charge of the body, completing the personal particulars.
steps.summary: The mortician fills in the non-medical information, obtains the medical certification or assurance that it was provided electronically, and files with the Secretary of Health.

steps.title: Burial-transit permit before disposition
steps.who: The mortician who first takes custody of the body obtains it.
steps.trigger: The death; needed before disposition or removal from the state.

deadline.text: within 72 hours after death and before final disposition or removal

steps.summary: No cemetery or crematory may accept a body without a burial-transit permit; on a multicopy certificate form, the designated copy signed by the physician or medical examiner is the permit.

steps.title: Cemetery returns the permit to the Secretary
steps.who: The person in charge of the cemetery or crematory (the mortician if there is none).
steps.summary: The disposition details are written on the permit and it is returned to the Secretary of Health.

steps.title: Certified or abridged copies to persons with a direct and tangible interest
steps.who: Surviving relatives, authorised representatives, beneficiaries, those establishing an estate, insurers and other payers of benefits, creditors, litigants, title transferors, and officials. Issued by the Department, local health departments and the Motor Vehicle Administration.
steps.summary: Each copy of a death certificate carries a notice about continuation of group health insurance. Local health departments and the MVA access certificates electronically from the Department.

steps.title: Insurers, pension payers and creditors may obtain a certified copy
steps.who: A person who paid, or is paying, insurance, pension, welfare or other benefits to the deceased or beneficiaries; a creditor; a person proving a beneficiary's death or clearing title.
steps.summary: Maryland regulation treats these private bodies as having a direct and tangible interest, so they can obtain the certificate themselves rather than waiting for the family; there is no push notification.

steps.title: Department of Health reports deaths to the State Board of Elections
steps.who: The Maryland Department of Health, to the State Administrator of Elections; individuals at least 16.
steps.trigger: Deaths reported since the last report.

deadline.text: in a format and at times prescribed by the State Board

steps.latencyNote: at times prescribed by the State Board; COMAR 33.05 sets none (md-el-3-504-a1)
steps.summary: Names and residence addresses of all deceased residents are reported to the State Administrator.

steps.title: State Administrator forwards death reports to local boards
steps.who: The State Administrator, to the local boards of elections.
steps.latencyNote: no time set; § 3-504(b)(1) and COMAR 33.05.06.05 read (md-el-3-504-b)
steps.summary: Local boards remove deceased voters; for SSA-sourced reports they first mail a notice giving two weeks to object.

steps.title: SSA death data for the voter roll
steps.who: The State Administrator arranges with SSA or an approved entity receiving SSA data.
steps.trigger: Reports of deceased Maryland residents aged 16 or more.
steps.latencyNote: no time set for SSA reports; § 3-504(a)(3) read (md-el-3-504-a3)
steps.summary: Captures deaths outside Maryland's own registry; the voter is removed unless someone objects within two weeks of the notice.

steps.title: Obituary or other reliable report triggers verification
steps.who: The local board's election director, on learning of an obituary or other reliable report.
steps.trigger: Obituary or reliable report of death.
steps.latencyNote: whenever a local board becomes aware; no time set (md-el-3-504-c1)
steps.summary: The election director mails a verification notice and may remove the voter on receiving verification.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: The mortician files within 72 hours after the death; medical certification is due within 24 hours.

informantDuty.note: The mortician completes the personal particulars and files; relatives supply information only.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate; the medical examiner takes charge only of deaths reportable under § 4-212(c).

electronicRegistration.note: Certification and transmission may be by an approved electronic process or by signature and paper; electronic filing is not mandated in the sections read.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the Department of Health holds the record and reports it to the bodies statutes name.

governmentPropagation.note: Registered deaths reach the voter roll automatically, and the MVA and local health departments can access certificates electronically to issue copies. No statutory death feed to MVA licence cancellation, the Comptroller or Medicaid was found. Federal feeds are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Certified or abridged copies only to persons with a direct and tangible interest under COMAR 10.03.01.08, which includes relatives, beneficiaries, benefit payers, creditors and officials.

gaps: privateSectorVerification is left to the us-federal layer (LADMF). Maryland's own route is narrow: COMAR lets insurers, benefit payers and creditors obtain a certified copy themselves (see md-insurer-copy).
Offence provisions for failing to file a death certificate (Health–General §§ 4-224 to 4-227 area) were not read.
No Transportation Article provision for MVA cancellation of a deceased person's licence on vital-records notice was searched; only the MVA's role as a certificate issuer was found.
No statute naming who may pronounce death (e.g., registered nurses in hospice) was found; § 5-202 sets only the criteria.
Whether Maryland's electronic death registration system transmits to SSA is not stated in the statutes read; the federal side belongs in us-federal.
regs.maryland.gov asks that the site not be scraped; only COMAR 10.03.01.08 and .09 were fetched individually.
